title: Claude Kennedy's Texas band, Lil Willie and Banjo Buck
summary: Kennedy's band came to Hollywood from Texas; Lil Willie was a trick drummer and Banjo Buck became a movie comedian.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: Yes. Well, that's another story. That's another story. But he came from there, and he was... So they had a very good... He had a big band, Claude did. Came to Hollywood, and he played all over Hollywood for dances. But the brand usually broke up. He had Lil' Willie and I playing drums, one of the greatest drummers in the whole West that they ever knew. Willie would throw those sticks up and caught them. He was one of the greatest for trick drumming. He eventually was put in Lucky Day, and he was a star of Lucky Day. One of the other, because I used him to throw those sticks up, you know, doing the overtures and so forth like that. Featuring the drummer. That was a big thing.
And he just was called Lil' Willie?

Lil' Willie. That's not a little... No name. Another one, saxophone player. It was called Big Willie. I forget. He played saxophone. Big Willie played tennis sax, and Lil' Willie played drum. I don't even know those guys. And Wallace played sax. They had a whole lot of the guys. Todd Kennedy, trumpet. They were the outstanding. They had a little short guy. Can't think of his name. They played. It was the same. Came all from Texas. And they stayed there. And they broke up after a while. After they were there. I got some of them into my band. But they were... It was a real great trumpet player.
You don't know Banjo Buck's right name.

Banjo... No. Banjo Buck... Banjo, fancy, got on his derby. And he worked in several pictures. He worked in the pictures. And he was a comedian. He worked in several of those colored pictures. You know, they had some black pictures at that time. Do you remember? I don't remember. And they had... And so Buck was in them. And he was gotten to be a movie star. And playing Banjo Buck. And he was... He got away from the band business. Start the acting. And I've never heard from him since. For a while he was in many pictures there. Comedy things. And that was about the... That was about as much as far as I remember. He played Banjo in the Victor record that I made. Called Mr. African. And another of them. I was trying to be a Duke Ellington style band. That's what I was trying to do. But I was a very poor... Which was good. Very good. Victor thought it was very good. But not in act place. You know. Because Duke had some great musicians with him. You had to have the fine musicians to have a great man like Duke. So you couldn't get one. No, I don't know.
